The parser now matches the whole string against an ordered `h`, `m`, `s` pattern with optional spaces between parts and decimal values allowed. It throws on empty input, negatives, unknown units, missing units, and out-of-order parts. The total is rounded to whole seconds, so `1.1h` gives 3960 rather than a floating-point value.

My edge-case checks (`1h 30m`, `1.5h`, `1h0m5s`, `-5m`, `30m1h`, `1 h`, `1h30`, empty string) were verified by reading the regex, not by running them, because the shell rejected the check commands. Only the three visible tests were actually run.
